summary: CardSorting — a reorderable list of cards, and the first component in this system whose whole contract is an interaction rather than a surface. Built without a drag library (ADR 0012, AGENTS.md independence), and that is not stubbornness: the accessible half of this pattern is the half a drag library does not solve, and it is most of the work. Reordering has THREE paths and all three are first-class rather than one real one and two fallbacks. A pointer drag; a keyboard lift-and-move on the handle (Space lifts, arrows move, Space drops, Escape restores the order from before the lift — a cancel that leaves the row where the arrows happened to take it is not a cancel); and a no-drag pointer path of click-the-handle-to-lift then click-a-row-to-place, which is what WCAG 2.5.7 (Dragging Movements) actually requires, since a keyboard alternative satisfies 2.1.1 and not 2.5.7. All three go through one move so they cannot diverge, and all three announce through one polite live region carrying the row's name, its new position, the total and the list's name — a reorder only sighted mouse users can perceive is not a reorder. Arrows deliberately do nothing until a row is lifted, so a stray arrow cannot silently reorder a list someone is reading, and so the keys do not fight the browser's own scrolling. The drag index is computed against the OTHER rows' midpoints rather than all of them: including the dragged row makes the target depend on where that row currently sits, which shifts the instant it moves — the index came out one short and the list juddered between two positions while the pointer stood still, caught by a test that dragged to a known midpoint and got the wrong neighbour. Two contract gaps the component exposed, both the 'an unlisted pair is an unchecked pair' failure: --ui-text-muted and --ui-border-focus had never been audited against --ui-bg-elevated, because nothing had drawn ink or a focus edge on that surface before; both are now in CONTRAST_PAIRS / NONTEXT_CONTRAST_PAIRS and measure 5.36:1 and 5.39:1 in light, 5.19:1 and 5.09:1 in dark. The lifted state is drawn as an OUTLINE rather than the sheet's border, so lifting a row cannot shift the layout by the pixel a resting row does not have.
